claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially has a single-phase, high-temperature disordered BCC structure.
Phase evolution in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is controlled by temperature-dependent chemical ordering.
Differential elemental diffusivities drive the proposed chemical ordering.
Al diffuses more slowly than the other constituents in this alloy.
Slow Al diffusion, together with associated local lattice distortions, nucleates ordered B2 domains during cooling or moderate thermal exposure.
The matrix remaining after partial ordering stays disordered BCC.
The B2 domains are nanoscale and form through localized Al segregation.
Cooling rates that permit sufficient atomic mobility allow local chemical partitioning and ordering.
Extremely rapid quenching suppresses diffusion and therefore suppresses significant local ordering.
Temperatures sufficiently high to maintain chemical disorder prevent the proposed B2 ordering.
At extremely low temperatures, kinetics are too slow for the proposed ordering mechanism to operate.
Subsequent moderate-temperature exposure modifies the volume fractions and stability of the ordered and disordered phases through additional ordering.
Moderate thermal exposure may produce a minor sigma phase.
Rapidly quenched baseline samples should retain a largely homogeneous, essentially single-phase disordered BCC structure.
Relative to the rapidly quenched baseline, slowly cooled or thermally exposed samples should exhibit detectable B2 ordering peaks in XRD.
Relative to the rapidly quenched baseline, slowly cooled or thermally exposed samples should contain nanoscale B2 precipitates observable by TEM or atom-probe tomography.
Slow cooling or moderate thermal exposure may generate minor secondary phases.
The predicted microstructural evolution should correlate with changes in mechanical properties.
Formation of B2 domains through Al segregation is supported by analogous high-entropy alloy systems.
The mechanism would be falsified if slow-cooled and thermally exposed samples show no significant phase-content or ordering difference from the rapidly quenched baseline.
